images.alt: A sandy-coloured wallaby sitting upright in dry grass
images.caption: An agile wallaby in dry grass, the most likely kadar 'plains wallaby' and by far the most recorded member of the family around Karma Waters.

images.alt: A grey kangaroo standing upright in tall dry grass under eucalypts, ears forward
images.caption: Eastern grey kangaroo in dry-season woodland grass, Carnarvon Gorge, central Queensland. The big grey of the open country, the likeliest julmbanu and mayarriji; ears forward means it has seen you.
images.credit: Photo: John Robert McPherson, via Wikimedia Commons

images.alt: A female grey kangaroo standing in open woodland with a joey's head showing from her pouch
images.caption: A female eastern grey with a joey in the pouch. 'The female ... is usually permanently pregnant except on the day she gives birth', and a mob always carries young.
images.credit: Photo: Donald Hobern from Copenhagen, Denmark, via Wikimedia Commons

images.alt: A dark wallaroo crouched at the edge of dry grass and timber on a stony slope
images.caption: Common wallaroo, the 'hill wallaroo', in granite country at Girraween, southern Queensland: dark, stocky, solitary and mostly out at night. The dark male is one candidate for nyarrkali 'black kangaroo'.
images.credit: Photo: John Robert McPherson, via Wikimedia Commons

images.alt: A pale wallaby with a white face stripe sitting in long dry grass in open woodland
images.caption: Whiptail or pretty-faced wallaby, the day-feeding wallaby of grassy hills, which gathers in mobs of up to 50 with lookouts posted. Twenty-eight Atlas records within 60 km of Karma Waters.
images.credit: Photo: John Robert McPherson, via Wikimedia Commons

images.alt: A tall reddish-tan kangaroo standing among burnt and regrowing woodland trees
images.caption: Antilopine kangaroo in regrowing woodland on Cape York Peninsula: the reddish-tan, long-limbed kangaroo of the lowland grass plains, recorded once within 30 km of the Karma Waters homestead.

images.alt: A small brown rock-wallaby sitting on a bare granite slab
images.caption: Mareeba rock-wallaby on granite near Mareeba. Its whole range runs 'from around Mount Garnet to the Mitchell River and Mount Carbine, and inland to Mungana, but only on the tops of a couple of mountain ranges'.

images.alt: A small dark wallaby with reddish legs on a forest track
images.caption: Red-legged pademelon at the rainforest edge on Mount Whitfield, Cairns: the most likely bimbarrbay 'scrub wallaby', a 2.5–7 kg animal that grazes the forest edges and bolts back into cover.
images.credit: Photo: Steve Fitzgerald, via Wikimedia Commons

images.alt: Two long narrow kangaroo hind-foot prints side by side in sand, with a tail mark between them
images.caption: Eastern grey kangaroo tracks in sand: the two long hind prints of a hop, each showing the big fourth toe and the shorter fifth that are 'the only ones that touch the ground', with the tail mark between.
images.credit: Photo: John Tann from Sydney, Australia, via Wikimedia Commons

images.alt: A rabbit-sized grey-brown rat-kangaroo on red earth at night, lit by a torch
images.caption: Rufous bettong at night in the Einasleigh country south of the Mitchell headwaters: the dictionary's jayju 'kangaroo rat', 'strictly nocturnal', which digs for roots and fungi and nests under thick cover by day.
images.credit: Photo: Greg Schechter from San Francisco, USA, via Wikimedia Commons

images.alt: A small grey rat-kangaroo standing upright in dry grass at night
images.caption: Northern bettong, endangered, with about a thousand left, in its Atherton Tableland stronghold. Two Atlas records sit inside the 60 km circle around Karma Waters.

images.alt: A tree-kangaroo sitting high in the canopy among leaves and vines
images.caption: Bennett's tree-kangaroo in the canopy on Eastern Kuku Yalanji country near the Daintree: murral, Nyungkul jarrabina. It lives only between Cooktown and the Daintree, and has no records on the Mitchell side.

images.alt: Line drawing of a long net held up between two end posts with forked intermediate supports, and a small drawing of the net rolled up for carrying
images.caption: Roth's Figs. 20–21, 1901: the Atherton kangaroo net of kurrajong fibre-twine, 16–18 feet between its side-supports (A), the top and bottom string (B) and the light forked supports (C) that stretch the centre higher than the sides; and the same net rolled on its side-supports to be slung over the shoulder. Public domain.
images.credit: Drawing: W. E. Roth, North Queensland Ethnography Bulletin No. 3 (1901), Figs. 20–21; scan via the Internet Archive

images.alt: Two photographs of a long cylindrical cane trap with a flared hooded mouth and a pointed end, seen from the side and from the mouth
images.caption: Roth's Figs. 22–23, 1901: the Atherton wallaby cage, the yingkar, of split lawyer cane, 4–4½ feet long with a pointed end and a half-funnel hood. Ten or twelve were laid along the wallaby pads, hood up, mouths hidden with bushes and bark, and a hard-pressed wallaby running head down jammed itself inside. Public domain.
images.credit: Photographs: W. E. Roth, North Queensland Ethnography Bulletin No. 3 (1901), Figs. 22–23; scan via the Internet Archive

images.alt: Line drawings of a long hunting net staked up on forked supports, three nets set as three sides of a square with kangaroo tracks entering, a bough alley, and hands weaving a net
images.caption: From Roth's Plate XI, 1897 (Boulia district, North-West Queensland): fig. 226, the emu-net rig that was 'quickly rigged up' across kangaroo pads to water, with its end posts, forked uprights and top string; fig. 232, 'three emu-nets placed in form of an enclosure, into which the kangaroos are driven' by beaters; fig. 228, a bough alley; fig. 227, weaving the net. Public domain.
images.credit: Drawing: W. E. Roth, Ethnological Studies among the North-West-Central Queensland Aborigines (1897), Plate XI; scan via the Internet Archive

images.alt: A wallaby standing upright on green grass
images.caption: Agile wallaby at Julatten, east of the Mitchell headwaters, showing the pale hip stripe and black-edged ears.
